subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This defines a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config/auth/provider writes, so automation cannot safely choose the fail-open/fail-closed behavior, recursion rules, metadata contract, or permanent SDK boundary.

options.title: Design the API in the RFC first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation only
options.body: Decide not to add a plugin veto and rescope or close this issue around schema validation, SecretRef preflight, baseHash, destructive-array, and agent-tool guards.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower gateway-tool guard for model-initiated config writes while accepting that other config writers remain outside the plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API in the RFC first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the clearest product-routing review and have nearby gateway config helper history.
